# Training Isometric Skills (Intensity and Volume)

volume or intensity which one is better to get better at calisthenics skills before i go further
 into my honest opinion about this topic let me explain what volume and intensity would be in
 context of calisthenics volume refers to how much or the quantity while intensity refers to how
 heavy or the quality so for example five sets of one front lever pull-up is an example of low volume
 high intensity work and five sets of five banded front lever pull-ups would be more of higher volume
 and lower intensity type of work we all know that we need a good mix of both volume and intensity
 for the good result but the question is which one is superior problem with intensity and volume is
 that they have invert relationship if you do high volume and high intensity it just means that
 intensity is not really that high because if it was high you wouldn't be able to do much volume
 the only way to do high volume and high intensity is to do a ton of sets with low rep range and to
 rest for three to five minutes between those sets i have tried it and to be honest the only
 thing that i can do is to do a ton of sets with low rep range and to rest for three to five minutes
 i got from it was a ton of frustration and bicep tendon irritation but it was fun and egotistical
 way to train indeed the issue was i trained too close to my one rep max so what is a one rep max
 it is simply a certain amount of weight you can lift for only one rep not to only one max effort
 rep you might ask what does that have to do with calisthenics well you see in calisthenics we are
 also doing weight training and usually we are working with pretty heavy loads considering
 the positions we need to hold that weight in because planche press is a very heavy weight
 exercise where you need to carry a certain amount of weight through a certain range of motion right
 the same as bench press you just need a different kind of strength isometric holds like maltese
 front lever and iron cross are just isometric portions of the full range of motion skills
 such as van gelder front lever pull and butterfly
 my point here is that isometric skills in calisthenics are just like isometric portions of repetitions in the gym just a hundred times harder of course this may seem like a total nonsense but this is what i believe in i devoted my time to learn about it and found out about one rep max chart it is a chart that tells us how many repetitions we can perform with certain percentage of one rep max i also find out the
 power letters don't go above 90 for majority of the time then i looked at what i'm doing maxing out my three seconds of maltese and five seconds of cross every single session wondering why i can't make any progress two seconds of isometric hold equals one rep so three seconds of max maltese hold is basically my one rep max so the whole time i'm training in the 95 to 100 of my rep max wondering what's wrong so i decide to drop my ego and go for a different approach where i will only
 perform movements and isometrics that are in my 80 to 90 percent rep max that is 8 to 16 seconds and 4 to 8 reps and that means that i need to only do maltese with the light band and so i train rings twice per week only around 10 sets of holds per week and i got from 8.5 seconds with band to 11 seconds of body with maltese hold in just five weeks
 the hard part was not doing any heavier loads until a predetermined day only with the band even though i could do it with my body weight and record cool clips and be cool but i really wanted to try this out and it worked amazingly and it also works for my man gary gary is a client
 of mine that wanted to work with me because he liked my planche ebook he applied what i wrote and made good progress so he also wanted to work with me one-on-one and he still continues to make great progress because he is an extremely patient and disciplined guy and it's so easy to work with him anyway all of this was just my observation and help of my good friend and coach david of course this is my opinion and you're allowed to disagree with me i do not have the last word on training calisthenics so just try it experiment learn and come up with a better conclusion
 but this is my conclusion change progressions of a skill that's in 80 to 90 percent of your one rep max use only the rubber band that takes away five to nine kilograms don't do more than 20 to 30 reps or 30 to 40 seconds of volume per session if it sounds like too little then decrease the rest between sets until you're doing it super efficiently and quickly apply progressive overload to your sets try to work a little bit harder every week but do not increase the volume thank you for watching and i hope you like this
